title: Open and closed subsets of a scheme correspond to idempotent global functions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. (a) For an idempotent $e\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ the set $U_e=\{x\in X: e_x\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal O_{X,x}\}$ equals $\{x: e_x=1\}$, is open and closed in $X$, and $X\setminus U_e=U_{1-e}$. (b) The map $e\mapsto U_e$ is a bijection from the set of idempotents of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ to the set of open and closed subsets of $X$; the inverse sends $U$ to the unique global section that restricts to $1$ on $U$ and to $0$ on $X\setminus U$. (c) For every morphism of schemes $g:Y\to X$ and every idempotent $e\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $g^\sharp(e)\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is idempotent and $U_{g^\sharp(e)}=g^{-1}(U_e)$.
